previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent DVT/PE on warfarin, dementia, and chronic GI issues was admitted for generalized weakness and suspected infection. She was found to have a supratherapeutic INR of 7.5, acute posthemorrhagic anemia (Hgb 7.3), and guaiac-positive stool, indicating GI bleeding. She received vitamin K, FFP, and packed red blood cells. A CT abdomen/pelvis showed no active bleed but confirmed diverticulosis. Due to family and PCP preference, endoscopy was deferred in favor of conservative management. She also had an Enterobacter UTI, treated with ceftriaxone initially and transitioned to oral Bactrim. A central line was placed for access. Her hemoglobin stabilized, INR normalized, and infection improved. Warfarin was restarted at 1 mg daily. She was discharged home with home health services, instructions to monitor for recurrent bleeding, and outpatient follow-up for INR checks.
